title: Nitrogen monoxide and ozone high in the air

stimulus.title: A two-step mechanism
stimulus.html:
High in the atmosphere, oxygen atoms and ozone react: O₃(g) + O(g) → 2 O₂(g). The reaction is slow on its own, but much faster when a small amount of nitrogen monoxide, NO, is present. A proposed mechanism with NO:

  1. NO(g) + O₃(g) → NO₂(g) + O₂(g)  (slow)
  2. NO₂(g) + O(g) → NO(g) + O₂(g)  (fast)

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that the two steps add up to the overall reaction.

rubric.point: Adds the steps and cancels NO and NO₂ to get O₃ + O → 2 O₂
accept: NO + O₃ + NO₂ + O → NO₂ + O₂ + NO + O₂; cancel NO and NO₂

parts.sample: Adding: NO + O₃ + NO₂ + O → NO₂ + O₂ + NO + O₂. NO and NO₂ appear on both sides and cancel, leaving O₃ + O → 2 O₂.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Identify the catalyst and the intermediate in the mechanism. Justify each choice.

rubric.point: NO is the catalyst: it is used in step 1 and regenerated in step 2 (present at the start, not consumed overall)
NO₂ is the intermediate: it is made in step 1 and used up in step 2

parts.sample: NO is the catalyst: it is a reactant in step 1 and is made again in step 2, so it is present at the start and is not used up overall. NO₂ is the intermediate: it is made in step 1 and used up in step 2, so it is not present at the start or the end.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Write the rate law for the overall reaction that is consistent with the mechanism, and explain your reasoning.

rubric.point: rate = k[NO][O₃], because step 1 is the slow (rate-determining) step and its rate law follows from its coefficients
accept: rate = k[NO][O₃] from the slow first step

parts.sample: rate = k[NO][O₃]. Step 1 is the slow, rate-determining step, and because it is an elementary step its rate law follows from its coefficients: one NO and one O₃ collide. O reacts only in the fast second step, so it does not appear.
